newsitem.title: UK: London gold market at standstill ahead of Easter.
newsitem.headline: London gold market at standstill ahead of Easter.

text.p: Precious metals prices were virtually static in early trading on Thursday ahead of the four-day Easter holiday weekend, dealers said.
Bullion was fixed sharply higher at $349.50 an ounce, compared to $346.05 previously, in the aftermath of a short-covering rally late on Wednesday.
But gold prices were drifting in a tiny $350.20-$349.60 range and looked set to oscillate around $350, dealers said.
However, the thin pre-holiday conditions left open the possibility of a sharp move if speculators in New York's Comex futures market made a play later in the day, a dealer noted.
"The market's dead in Europe but that could change if- the fund activity we've been seeing in New York lately comes in later," he said.
The market appeared to have digested late Wednesday's news that size of the massive Busang gold deposit in Indonesia may have been overstated.
A shortcovering rally had sent prices shooting up some $5 on Wednesday afternoon, from a low of around $346, after a test of key support around $345/$346 held.
The rise was later fuelled by news that tests of the Busang deposit showed insignificant amounts of gold.
"Gold certainly rallied about $1 on that news, which was a valid move in a short market," a dealer said.
"But fundamentally it doesn't change the fact that gold is still in a downtrend."
Later in Hong Kong spot gold ended off highs as players liquidated positions.
The other precious metals markets were equally lifeless early in the day and showed little sign of moving out of well-worn price ranges.
Silver prices were unchanged at $5.14/$5.16 an ounce after trading in a two-cent range all day.
Platinum was $1.00 firmer at $373.50/$374.50, while palladium was unchanged at $145.00/$146.00.
The market was in a holding pattern pending fresh news on delayed supply talks between major producer Russia and importer Japan, dealers said.
